notes:
**A share button is no longer counted as a broken outbound link.**

Nearly every page carries "share this on X", and X answers an automated request
with a 404 — including for its own bare `x.com/intent/tweet` endpoint, which is
plainly alive and returns 200 to a browser. So the status code cannot tell a
refusal from a dead page, and share buttons were being reported as broken links
on every page that has one. On a cathedral-sized site audited this week, twelve
of sixteen "broken outbound links" were one share widget.

Share buttons for X, Facebook, LinkedIn, Pinterest, Reddit, WhatsApp, Telegram,
Tumblr, Bluesky and Threads are no longer counted as outbound links at all —
they point back at your own page, and you cannot fix how X answers a crawler.
Links to those same sites that are real references still are.

A **402 Payment Required** now reads as "could not be checked" rather than
"broken", alongside 400, 401, 403 and 429. It says the server wants paying, not
that the page is gone.

**"Change the sample text" is an instruction, not leftover template text.**

A guide to making posters was reported, at high severity, as having unfinished
content live — because it tells readers to change the sample text in a template.
Docket already recognised "replace the sample text" as commentary; it now knows
the rest of that family, including change, edit, swap, customise and overwrite.

**"St" is also how you abbreviate Saint.**

A church's site had no postal address on it, and Docket found three — reading
"2017 This summer St Albans Diocese" and "and a highway shall be there" as
street addresses, then switching a whole lane of local-business checks on. An
abbreviated street type followed by a name is now read as a saint, and a street
name has to be more than one letter. Full street words are untouched, and
`1600 Pennsylvania Ave NW` still reads as an address.
